Quick Summary

Soul on Ice (1968) is an autobiographical work by Eldridge Cleaver, a prominent Black militant in the United States. The book is a collection of essays detailing Cleaver's personal evolution and his experiences with racism in America. Cleaver, who spent significant time in correctional institutions, began writing these essays while in prison, drawing inspiration from Malcolm X. 1
The publication of Soul on Ice , initially in Ramparts magazine, contributed to his parole in 1966. The book became a significant statement of Black alienation and established Cleaver as a leading Black radical voice. Cleaver was also a minister of information for the Black Panther Party. 1

Eldridge Cleaver

Eldridge Cleaver and his wife, Kathleen Eldridge Cleaver (left) and his wife, Kathleen.
Eldridge Cleaver (born 1935, Wabbaseka, near Little Rock, Arkansas, U.S.—died May 1, 1998, Pomona, California) was an American Black militant whose autobiographical volume Soul on Ice (1968) is a classic statement of Black alienation in the United States.
Cleaver was an inmate of correctional institutions in California almost constantly from his junior high school days until 1966 for crimes ranging from possession of marijuana to assault with intent to murder. While in prison, he supplemented his incomplete education with wide reading and became a follower of the Black Muslim separatist Malcolm X . He also began writing the essays that would eventually be collected in Soul on Ice , and whose publication in Ramparts magazine helped him win parole in 1966.
Eldridge Cleaver Eldridge Cleaver, 1968. (more)
After being paroled, Cleaver met Huey Newton and Bobby Seale, who had just founded the Black Panther Party in Oakland, California. Cleaver soon became the party’s minister of information. The publication in 1968 of Soul on Ice , a collection of angry memoirs in which Cleaver traced his political evolution while denouncing American racism, made him a leading Black radical spokesman. In April 1968, however, he was involved in a shoot-out in Oakland between Black Panthers and police that left one Panther dead and Cleaver and two police officers wounded.
